title: Randomized exponential-time decision predicate
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. For every Boolean string $x$, the machine's runtime is at most $T(|x|)$. If $x\in L$, then for every rational $\varepsilon>0$ there is a number of random choice bits $t$ for which the probability that the machine halts with output `[true]` is at least $2/3-\varepsilon$. If $x\notin L$, then every choice-bit string $w$ whose run halts produces output `[false]`.
